subject: TTFT & streaming SLOs — post-demo recap + next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samara Khan <samara.khan@atlasai.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: TTFT & streaming SLOs — post-demo recap + next steps

Thanks again for taking the call today, Samara — great to meet the AtlasAI team. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Summary of requirements (from today's demo):
- Primary goal: sub-300ms Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) for short/interactive chat prompts (<=128 input tokens).
- Target p95/p99 for first token: p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 450ms (you mentioned p99 tolerance up to ~500ms during heavy bursts).
- Concurrency & throughput: 100 concurrent chat sessions during peak, with sustained ~30 RPS and burst up to 150 RPS for short windows.
- Streaming behavior: must support streaming responses to client (SSE or WebSocket). First chunk should arrive quickly (goal: first chunk <= 200ms), then subsequent chunks target cadence ~100-200ms depending on model latency. Chunk sizes ~20-40 tokens preferred to keep UX smooth.
- Connection expectations: long-lived WebSocket preferred by product team for multiplexing, but SSE is acceptable if cadence and reconnect behavior meet SLAs.
- Failure modes: graceful fallback to non-streaming mode if streaming fails; clear client-side timeouts.

Next steps (proposed):
1) I'll send over a short SLO worksheet (attached) to capture exact p50/p95/p99 targets and traffic profiles for each workload pattern.
2) Schedule a 60-min tech deep-dive with your infra engineer + our SE (Rishi) to go over streaming options (SSE vs WebSocket), chunk cadence tuning, and required networking config (keep-alive, proxies, and LB timeouts).
3) Run a small PoC on Dedicated capacity that mirrors your peak concurrency for 48 hours to validate TTFT at scale.

Can you confirm the p95/p99 numbers above and share a rough peak-hour RPS distribution? I can get the calendar invite out once you confirm availability for next week.

Attachments: AtlasAI_TTFT_requirements.xlsx (SLO worksheet)

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0172

From: Samara Khan <samara.khan@atlasai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming SLOs — post-demo recap + next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is a helpful summary. Confirming details from our end: 
- p95 TTFT target: 200-250ms (hard requirement for interactive chat).
- p99 TTFT target: ideally <= 450ms, we can accept up to 500ms during extreme bursts but prefer under 450ms.
- Typical workload: 30-50 RPS sustained globally, peak-hour bursts up to 150 RPS (lasting ~5-10 minutes).
- Concurrency: we expect ~100 active concurrent sessions during peak, with message sizes averaging 80-150 tokens.
- Streaming: product prefers WebSocket for bi-directional control (typing indicators, cancel). Cadence target: first chunk within 150-200ms, then every ~120-160ms. We are sensitive to initial TTFT more than later chunk cadence.

I'll attach our SLO workbook with a couple of traffic profiles and a small synthetic latency histogram from our internal tests.

Availability for tech deep-dive: Jun 7 or Jun 9 between 10:00-15:00 PT. Prefer Jun 7 morning if possible.

Attachments: AtlasAI_TTFT_requirements.xlsx, sse_vs_websocket_comparison.pdf

Cheers,
Samara Khan
Head of Product
AtlasAI
samara.khan@atlasai.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Samara Khan <samara.khan@atlasai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming SLOs — post-demo recap + next steps

Thanks Samara — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A few quick technical follow-ups before the deep-dive so we can prep tests and PoC config: 

1) Models & sequence lengths
- Which model family(s) do you plan to use in prod for chat? (e.g., Llama-2/Redwood-{size}, open LLMs, or a hosted foundation model). The per-token generation cost and latency profile changes a lot by model size.
- Max response length we should simulate? You mentioned avg 80-150 tokens but what's the 95th percentile?

2) Network topology and clients
- Will clients be in browsers (WebSocket/SSE) behind enterprise proxies? Any known proxy timeout issues (e.g., App Gateway dropping idle connections at 60s)?

3) Desired p50/p95/p99 numeric SLOs for throughput tests
- You shared p95/p99 for TTFT; can you share p50 (we typically target <120ms for p50 on interactive flows).

4) Chunking behavior
- Do you want fixed-size chunks (e.g., 32 tokens) or time-based flush (first chunk asap then flush every ~120ms)? Our runtime supports both; time-based flush typically yields lower TTFT for the first chunk.

5) Measurement & telemetry
- We'll provide an SDK snippet for client-side measurement (first byte, first token, chunk cadence). Would you like server-side traces pushed to your Datadog/Prometheus?

Example SSE curl (for reference)
curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' \
  -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-medium","input":"hi"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream

If you can send the model family and p50 target (even approximate) I can prepare an initial PoC config and test harness for Jun 7. We're happy to provision a dedicated capacity test that mirrors your concurrency/burst profile.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer, Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

From: Samara Khan <samara.khan@atlasai.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming SLOs — post-demo recap + next steps

Thanks Rishi — answers below inline: 
1) Models: We'll start with an open LLM variant (Redwood-equivalent medium) for the PoC; in prod we may evaluate larger sizes for quality but want to validate TTFT on the medium class first. 95th percentile response length ~300 tokens (we'll include a column in the attached workbook).
2) Clients: Browser-based WebSocket clients behind corporate proxies (NGINX, corporate gateways). Some proxies have 60s idle drop; we'll test keep-alive/ping interval during PoC.
3) p50 target: aiming for p50 TTFT <= 120ms for the interactive flow.
4) Chunking: prefer time-based flush (first chunk asap, subsequent flush every ~120-160ms). Please default to time-based in the PoC.
5) Telemetry: yes — please push server-side traces to our Datadog account (we'll share a read-only API key ahead of the PoC). Also include client SDK snippet.

We can confirm the Jun 7 slot — morning PT works. Looking forward to the deep-dive and PoC details.

Best,
Samara
